coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: Easy 8–10 miles, Z2 (140–150 bpm), no vert work. You're in taper week 3 with a recovery score of 42/100 and last night's sleep was 5.55h—both red flags. Your resting HR is 2 bpm elevated (64 vs. 62.2 baseline), signaling incomplete recovery. This is a hold-the-fitness day, not a stimulus day. Keep it conversational, stay below 150 bpm, and treat this as a shakeout to move the legs and accumulate time on feet without demanding glycogen or neuromuscular recovery. You have 54 days to race; burnout now costs you the Alps.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Prioritize carbohydrate intake over the next 48 hours—aim for 7–8g/kg bodyweight daily to top off liver and muscle glycogen before your next hard block. During today's easy run, consume 30–40g simple carbs (sports drink, gels) per hour if the run exceeds 90 min. Post-run, eat 1.2g carbs + 0.3g protein per kg bodyweight within 30 min. Your sleep debt is real; don't compound it with caloric deficit. Eat slightly above maintenance today and tomorrow.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Last night's 5.55h is unacceptable for taper phase. Alpine 50Ks demand full CNS readiness at kilometer 35 when your quads are screaming on 30° climbs—sleep deprivation will wreck pacing judgment and muscular resilience. Tonight, target 8–9 hours in a cool (16–18°C), dark room. If travel or work is fragmenting your sleep, prioritize a 90-min nap this afternoon. Your recovery score of 42 and elevated RHR suggest accumulated fatigue; sleep is the only tool that fixes this. Non-negotiable.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: You're 8 weeks out and in taper—expect the mind to play tricks ("I'm losing fitness," "I should do more"). You're not. Your last three runs (17.16, 11.02, 10.21 miles) show strong aerobic fitness and the vertical work is locked in. The taper's job is to let your body absorb the training stimulus and repair. Treat this week as a confidence builder, not a fitness probe. Trust the training, sleep hard, and show up to Kranjska Gora fresh.
